# Street traffic test footage

- Title: **Street traffic** (San Francisco, 28 May 2011).
- Author / attribution: **Editor**, https://www.youtube.com/user/Editor
- Original publication: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_7sCYyxw4Ic
- Source and license record: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Street_traffic.webm
- Original media: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/70/Street_traffic.webm
- License: **Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported**, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
- Retrieved: 2026-09-30.

Local modifications: full clip transcoded from WebM to H.264 MP4, resized to 768×432, and audio removed. No scene content was added or generated. Three JPEGs were extracted at 3, 15, and 28 seconds from the local MP4. The original is about 35 seconds; this is street-level traffic footage, not an onboard dashcam recording.

Files: `street-traffic.mp4`, `street-traffic-03s.jpg`, `street-traffic-15s.jpg`, `street-traffic-28s.jpg`. Attribution and license also apply to the extracted frames. No endorsement is implied.

## Visual reference notes, written before model testing

- **3 s:** several buses, a foreground truck marked SKYLINE, rail tracks, overhead wires, trees, and a red signal near the upper right.
- **15 s:** a central bus, red taxi at lower right, cyclist with a red helmet at lower left, partial streetcar at left, and a red signal near upper right.
- **28 s:** pedestrians in the roadway farther back, several buses, rail tracks, partial streetcar at left, and a cropped red-helmeted cyclist at the bottom edge. Different signals show different colors; a generic claim that all traffic lights are red/green would be misleading.

These are human visual reference notes for selected frames, not exhaustive annotations or an ADAS benchmark. A single image does not establish vehicle speed, trajectory, or collision risk.
